evidence: Scope: all three scored dimensions are batched (judge.toml [judge] mode = "batched", [scoring] aggregation = "weighted_mean"): functional 44 binary, polish 5 binary, visual 5 likert. Gates render/constraints use aggregation = "all_pass" (gates/*/judge.toml:15) and are exempt. Independence wording present in every scored prompt: (1) tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles.' plus re-setup instruction for failed setup steps (line 13), line 7 'give that criterion its lowest score ... and move on', line 23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', line 53 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' (2) tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; line 7 'move on'; line 18 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' (3) tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.'; line 16 same preservation sentence. No stop-on-first-failure wording: grep for stop/abort/first fail/skip-the-rest across scored prompt.md and judge.toml found none. The only all-or-nothing rules are the global browser/backend gate (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which the template itself prescribes ('If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension', template scored/*/prompt.md) and the workbook row targets per-criterion failure, not the gate. Cross-row coupling scan (tomllib parse of all 54 scored criteria): references to sibling rows are dedupe pointers ('belongs to hro_bulk_places', 'graded only in hro_undo_conflict', 'graded only in hro_pol_session_resume'), which reduce double deduction rather than chain failures. hro_refusal_status says 'a replay that was accepted is deducted only in its own row ... If none of these replays was refused, this row is 0' - this depends on the observed replay responses (no refusal exists whose status could be checked), not on a sibling verdict, so one sibling failure does not zero it; partial refusals still score it. Polish rows' 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0' are each row's own observation. Attempted counterexamples: (a) broken app whose single-card move into a full Interview is accepted: functional hro_interview_full fails, but prompt line 13 forbids using that as evidence against hro_bulk_places/hro_undo_full, which have their own observations; (b) app whose job-open setup breaks mid-protocol: line 13 tells the judge to set up again on a new job where possible and continue, so unrelated rows (conversations, unread, candidate view) still score; (c) conforming app with one cosmetic visual weakness: visual:12 scores each likert row independently. No path found where one criterion's miss zeroes the rest beyond the template-sanctioned gate. Compared with template: task prompts replace the template's 'Independent scoring'/'Guardrails' sections with equivalent or stronger wording; no regression. Limits: this is a static prompt-wording row. raw-evidence-index.json scope states full configured judge runs are absent, so actual judge adherence to continue-after-failure is not measured; the workbook row and skill reference (quality-checks.md:156-159) define this check on prompt wording, and check-batched-independence-wording.py (deterministic reviewer's domain) owns the mechanical version - it was not executed here. Frozen-task hash not recomputed by me; reviewed the frozen copy named in the assignment.
